title: Single-file components with declared props
summary: Build a Vue single-file component that declares its props and renders them in the template.

scenario.briefing: A campus storefront needs a product card. The card currently hardcodes demo values instead of accepting data from its parent.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Use a script setup block with the TypeScript language attribute.
Call defineProps with an inline type that has name and price.
Assign the macro result to props and read props.name in the template.

misconceptions.feedback: Props are read-only. Emit an event so the parent updates its own state.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Assigning to a prop warns and leaves the parent's value unchanged; emit an event instead.

misconceptions.description: Copying demo values into the component instead of declaring props.
misconceptions.feedback: Hardcoded values ignore the parent. Declare the data contract with defineProps.
misconceptions.testDescription: The component declares typed props with defineProps.

misconceptions.description: Believing a child assignment updates the parent.
misconceptions.feedback: Vue props are read-only. The child emits an event and the parent changes its own state.

sections.title: One file, three blocks
sections.body: A single-file component keeps its script, template, and optional styles together. The script setup block runs once per component instance and exposes bindings to the template.

sections.title: Props are declared, not copied
sections.body: defineProps is a compile-time macro that declares the values a parent may pass. Props are read-only inside the child.

sections.title: Templates render reactive values
sections.body: A template expression re-evaluates when the values it reads change. Reading through the props object keeps the binding visible.

vocabulary.definition: A .vue file that groups script, template, and style blocks.
A compile-time macro that declares a component's props.
A binding inside the template that is evaluated against the component scope.

steps.title: Declare props in a single-file component
steps.prompt: Edit ProductCard.vue. Declare name and price with defineProps, then render both in the template. Format the price with two decimals.

tests.description: The component declares typed props with defineProps.
The template renders the name and a two-decimal price.

hints: Replace the demo constants with a defineProps call.
Declare name as string and price as number in the generic.
Read props.name and props.price in the template.
Format the price with props.price.toFixed(2) and remove the TODO.

steps.title: Props in templates

statements.label: defineProps declares the values a component accepts from its parent.
A child component may assign directly to a prop to update the parent.
A single-file component groups script, template, and style in one file.
Template expressions read from the component's reactive scope.
Every prop must be copied into a global store before it can render.

steps.explanation: defineProps makes the component's data contract explicit. The child reads props and renders them, while the parent remains the owner of the values.
hints: Check whether each statement treats props as read-only.
Remember that defineProps is compiled, not a runtime function imported from Vue.
Check the claims about template scope and single-file structure.
Select only the statements that match Vue's component model.
